universal.label: Unified Emergency Dispatch (Police, Fire, EMS)
universal.description: Universal emergency number across the United States for immediate Police, Fire, and Ambulance dispatch via voice or Text-to-911.

categories.name: Police & Public Safety
categories.description: Immediate law enforcement, active threat response, and highway patrol.

numbers.label: Police Emergency Dispatch
numbers.audience: Anyone witnessing or experiencing a crime in progress, threat to life, or violent incident.
numbers.whenToUse: Call or text 911 immediately when safety is at risk. Enhanced 911 (E911) transmits mobile location to the nearest Public Safety Answering Point.

categories.name: Medical & Crisis
categories.description: Emergency Medical Services (EMS), poison control, and suicide/mental health crisis lifelines.

numbers.label: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) & Ambulance
numbers.audience: Anyone experiencing chest pain, stroke symptoms, severe bleeding, unconsciousness, or trauma.
numbers.whenToUse: Call immediately when rapid paramedic intervention and ambulance transport are required.

numbers.label: Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
numbers.audience: Anyone experiencing suicidal thoughts, mental health crisis, substance use distress, or emotional overwhelm.
numbers.whenToUse: Call or text 988 for free, confidential support from trained crisis counselors. Veterans can press 1 after dialing 988.

numbers.label: America's Poison Centers Helpline
numbers.audience: Parents, caregivers, or individuals exposed to toxic substances, medication overdose, or chemical splashes.
numbers.whenToUse: Call immediately if someone swallows or inhales a suspected poison but is conscious and breathing (call 911 if unconscious).

categories.name: Fire & Rescue
categories.description: Structural fire response, hazmat incidents, and technical rescue.

numbers.label: Fire Department & Hazmat Dispatch
numbers.audience: General public reporting structure fires, wildfires, carbon monoxide alarms, or gas leaks.
numbers.whenToUse: Evacuate the area first, then dial 911 from a safe distance.

categories.name: Women & Child Safety
categories.description: National domestic violence, sexual assault, and child abuse protection hotlines.

numbers.label: National Domestic Violence Hotline
numbers.audience: Survivors of intimate partner violence, concerned friends/family, and individuals seeking safe shelter.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 1-800-799-SAFE (7233) or text 'START' to 88788 for confidential safety planning and local shelter referrals.

numbers.label: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
numbers.audience: Children at risk of abuse, parents in crisis, and mandated reporters or bystanders.
numbers.whenToUse: Call or text when a child is facing abuse or neglect and needs crisis intervention or CPS routing.

categories.name: Disaster, Road & Cyber
categories.description: FEMA disaster relief, state highway assistance, and CISA cyber incident reporting.

numbers.label: FEMA Disaster Assistance Helpline
numbers.audience: Residents and families impacted by federally declared hurricanes, wildfires, floods, or tornadoes.
numbers.whenToUse: Call after immediate life safety is secured to register for emergency housing, grants, and disaster recovery aid.

numbers.label: State DOT Highway & Roadside Info
numbers.audience: Motorists needing real-time highway closures, winter storm road conditions, or non-emergency DOT motorist assist.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 511 on interstate and state highways for non-life-threatening roadside assistance and traffic advisories (call 911 for crashes).

numbers.label: CISA Central Cyber Incident Reporting
numbers.audience: Organizations, critical infrastructure operators, and individuals reporting severe ransomware or cyber attacks.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 1-844-SAY-CISA to report critical cybersecurity incidents or active ransomware attacks.
